name: the-window-stays-a-window-after-a-reveal
description: The reporter cannot click anywhere in the browser and the window manager no longer identifies the window. Both symptoms point at the reveal panel: it is a child window, it is non-activating, and the grip band the parent puts under it is a full-height view that claims events. This drives a whole reveal cycle and then asks the two questions a broken build cannot answer - is there still one standard window, and does a click on the page still land.

actions.note: first paint, and the sidebar announces itself
the sidebar is alive before any of this
collapse, so the edge zone arms
leave for the page, so the panel dismisses through its own rule
past the 280ms grace and the 240ms slide, so the panel is down and its contents are back in the pane
dock the pane again, which is the state the reporter opens in

assertions.label: one-standard-window-remains
assertions.desc: A window the manager cannot identify does not come back as AXStandardWindow. A second one would mean the panel is being counted as a window of its own.
Cmd+Q is itself a click-free proof that the window still takes key input
